title: What fit and proper requirements apply to pension fund managers under IORP II?
seoTitle: IORP II fit and proper requirements
description: IORP II Article 22 fit and proper rules for pension funds, key functions and outsourcing, with Portugal's ASF rules in Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R.
shortAnswer: Article 22 of the IORP II Directive (EU) 2016/2341 requires institutions for occupational retirement provision (IORPs) to ensure that the people who effectively run them, the holders of key functions, and anyone to whom a key function is outsourced are fit and proper. Fitness is collective for those running the fund and individual for key function holders. In Portugal, the Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões (ASF) adds detailed rules in Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R.
keyTakeaways: Article 22(1) sets three fitness tests: collective adequacy for persons who effectively run the IORP, professional qualifications for actuarial and internal audit holders, and adequate qualifications for other key function holders. Propriety means good repute and integrity.
The requirement extends to persons or entities to which a key function has been outsourced under Article 31, and competent authorities must be able to assess compliance (Article 22(2)).

Article 21(6) requires at least two persons to effectively run an IORP, unless the authority allows one after a reasoned assessment; Article 24 requires risk management, internal audit and, where applicable, actuarial key functions.
Member States had to transpose IORP II by January 13, 2019 (Article 64), and the Commission's review under Article 62 was due by January 13, 2023.

In Portugal, the pension funds regime (RJFP) approved by Law 27/2020 sets qualification and integrity requirements, and ASF Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R requires reassessment of fitness at least every five years and lists eight areas of collective board knowledge.
jurisdiction: European Union (IORP II Directive (EU) 2016/2341 as transposed in each Member State), with Portugal as a verified national example
regulator: National competent authorities for occupational pensions, including the Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões (ASF) in Portugal, coordinated by the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
appliesTo: Institutions for occupational retirement provision (IORPs) registered or authorized in an EU Member State
Members of the management or supervisory body and other persons who effectively run the IORP
Holders of the risk management, internal audit and actuarial key functions
Service providers performing outsourced key functions; in Portugal, pension fund management companies (sociedades gestoras de fundos de pensões)

sections.heading: What does Article 22 of IORP II require?

blocks.text: Article 22 requires Member States to make IORPs ensure that three groups of people are fit and proper when carrying out their tasks: those who effectively run the IORP, those who carry out key functions, and persons or entities to which a key function has been outsourced. The text is from [Directive (EU) 2016/2341](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32016L2341) on EUR-Lex, as at November 2026.

blocks.text: Article 22(2) requires Member States to ensure competent authorities can assess whether these persons meet the requirements. Articles 22(3) to 22(6) deal with cross-border proof: a home Member State that requires proof of good repute or no previous bankruptcy must accept a judicial record extract or equivalent document from another Member State, or a declaration on oath where none is issued, presented within three months of issue.

sections.heading: Which key functions does IORP II require?

blocks.text: Article 24(1) requires a risk management function, an internal audit function and, where applicable, an actuarial function. Article 6 defines a key function as "a capacity to undertake practical tasks comprising the risk management function, the internal audit function, and the actuarial function."

items: **Combining functions:** a single person or unit may carry out more than one key function, except internal audit, which must be independent of the others (Article 24(2)).

**Separation from the sponsor:** the key function holder must be different from the one carrying out a similar function in the sponsoring undertaking, unless the Member State allows the same person and the IORP explains how it manages conflicts (Article 24(3)).

**Escalation duty:** key function holders report material findings to the management or supervisory body and must inform the competent authority if the body does not take timely remedial action on a substantial compliance risk or a significant breach (Article 24(4) and (5)), with legal protection for doing so (Article 24(6)).
**Management structure:** at least two persons must effectively run the IORP, although a Member State may allow one person on a reasoned assessment by the competent authority (Article 21(6)).

**Written policies:** risk management, internal audit and, where relevant, actuarial and outsourced activities, approved by the management or supervisory body and reviewed at least every three years (Article 21(3)).

blocks.text: The three year policy review cycle differs from Solvency II, where insurers review written policies at least annually. The page on [Solvency II fit and proper requirements](/regulations/solvency-ii-fit-and-proper-requirements) sets out the insurance regime for comparison.

sections.heading: How do fit and proper rules apply when a key function is outsourced?

blocks.text: The outsourced provider must meet the same fit and proper requirements, and the IORP stays fully responsible. Article 22(1) names persons or entities to which a key function has been outsourced, and Article 31(2) states that IORPs remain fully responsible for compliance when they outsource key functions or other activities.

Article 31(3) bars outsourcing that impairs the quality of the system of governance, unduly increases operational risk, or impairs the competent authority's ability to monitor compliance. Many smaller IORPs outsource actuarial or internal audit work, so the fit and proper file for the provider's named individuals is part of the IORP's own evidence.

sections.heading: When did IORP II apply, and is it under review?

blocks.text: Member States had to bring transposing laws into force by January 13, 2019, when the earlier Directive 2003/41/EC was repealed (Articles 64 and 65). Article 62 required the Commission to review the Directive and report on its implementation and effectiveness by January 13, 2023, including the adequacy of the Directive from a prudential and governance point of view.

National rules continue to develop on top of the Directive. Portugal's ASF states in the preamble of Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R that it took account of EIOPA's technical advice on the review of Directive (EU) 2016/2341. Any later amendment to the Directive would need checking on EUR-Lex before relying on this page.

sections.heading: How does Portugal apply IORP II fit and proper rules?

blocks.text: Portugal applies the requirements through the legal regime for pension funds and their management entities (RJFP), approved by Law 27/2020 of July 23, and through ASF regulations. Articles 110 to 113 of the RJFP set the selection and assessment policy and the qualification and integrity requirements, and the ASF's [Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R of August 20](https://www.asf.com.pt/supervis%C3%A3o/governa%C3%A7%C3%A3o/governa%C3%A7%C3%A3o-de-entidades-gestores-de-fundos-de-pens%C3%B5es) on the governance system of pension fund management entities adds detail.

items: **Selection and assessment policy (Article 16):** must describe how persons subject to ASF registration under Article 73(1) of the RJFP are identified, which situations trigger reassessment of qualification and integrity, with reassessment at least every five years, and how other relevant staff outside Articles 112 and 113 of the RJFP are assessed.

**Collective knowledge (Article 17(2)):** the management body must collectively hold adequate qualification, experience and knowledge in at least eight areas: pension fund and financial markets; strategy and business model; governance system; financial and actuarial analysis; legal and regulatory framework, including anti-money laundering; information and communication technologies; distribution; and market conduct.
**Investment knowledge (Article 17(3)):** knowledge of investments, asset management and risk mitigation must be considered within the markets area.
**Integrity (Article 18):** possible periods of disqualification attached to offenses committed must be taken into account.

**Accumulation of roles (Article 19):** accumulation of responsibilities by a board member, especially for distribution and market conduct, must be weighed in the assessment report, including conflicts of interest and availability.

blocks.text: Under Article 123, Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R entered into force 60 days after publication, with listed provisions taking effect from January 1, 2025. Prior registration for regulated functions is handled under Norma Regulamentar 9/2023-R, and the ASF publishes guidance on assessment and prior registration in Circular 2/2023 of February 14. Other Portuguese governance duties, such as [anti-money laundering training](/regulations/portugal-aml-law-training-requirements), sit alongside these rules.

blocks.text: Collective knowledge only stays adequate if members keep learning as rules change. The guides on [building a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) and [reporting training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board) cover how to keep that evidence current. For a non-EU comparison, see the Australian superannuation regime on the page on [APRA SPS 510 fit and proper training](/regulations/apra-superannuation-sps-510-fit-and-proper-training).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each required knowledge area, such as the eight areas in Portugal's Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R, to roles and assessment points, so board development and key function training link to the gaps they close. The fit and proper file then shows current evidence of collective and individual fitness.

faqs.q: Does every board member of an IORP need pensions expertise?
faqs.a: No. For persons who effectively run the IORP, Article 22(1)(a)(i) requires qualifications, knowledge and experience that are collectively adequate. Individual members can bring different expertise, provided the group as a whole covers what sound and prudent management needs, and that coverage is documented.

faqs.q: Can one person hold several key functions in an IORP?
faqs.a: Yes, except internal audit. Article 24(2) allows a single person or organizational unit to carry out more than one key function, but the internal audit function must be independent from the other key functions.

faqs.q: How is IORP II different from Solvency II on fit and proper?
faqs.a: Both require fitness and propriety, but IORP II states the fitness test separately for those running the fund (collective) and for key function holders (individual), names outsourced providers directly in Article 22(1), and reviews written policies at least every three years rather than annually.

faqs.q: Who supervises pension funds in Portugal?
faqs.a: The Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões (ASF) supervises pension funds and their management entities, and issues regulations such as Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R on the governance system of pension fund management entities under powers in the RJFP approved by Law 27/2020.

factCheck.claim: IORP II Article 22(1): fit and proper for persons who effectively run the IORP (collectively adequate), actuarial and internal audit holders (professional qualifications), other key function holders, and outsourced key function providers under Article 31; proper means good repute and integrity; 22(2) authority assessment; 22(3) to (6) cross-border proof within three months.

IORP II Article 6 definition of key function; Article 24(1) risk management, internal audit and where applicable actuarial; 24(2) internal audit independent; 24(3) sponsor separation; 24(4) to (6) reporting and escalation with legal protection.

IORP II Article 21(3) written policies reviewed at least every three years; 21(6) at least two persons effectively run the IORP; Article 31(2) and (3) outsourcing responsibility and limits; Article 64 transposition by 13 January 2019; Article 62 review by 13 January 2023.

ASF Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R: RJFP approved by Law 27/2020 of 23 July; Articles 110 to 113 RJFP; Article 16 selection and assessment policy with reassessment at least every five years; Article 17(2) eight collective knowledge areas and 17(3) investments; Article 18 disqualification periods; Article 19 accumulation of roles; Article 123 entry into force 60 days after publication, listed provisions from 1 January 2025; preamble references EIOPA technical advice on IORP II review and NR 9/2023-R.

ASF fit and proper page lists Circular 2/2023 of 14 February with ASF guidelines on assessment and prior registration for regulated functions; governance page lists Norma Regulamentar 6/2024-R of 20 August on governance of pension fund management entities.
